Short answers:
- We do banded pricing for premium support: a retainer + response SLA, and we apply credits differently depending on whether it's availability (uptime) vs operational throughput (rate/latency).
- For planned peak windows we offer an "uplift window" add-on (timeboxed extra coverage) that changes both response SLAs and the credit calculation to protect you during predictable spikes.

1) expected baseline RPS and expected peak RPS during a 1–7 day event?

Hi all —

Draft banded pricing below (high level). This is intentionally conservative so we can tighten with exact traffic numbers. All numbers are USD monthly-equivalent for clarity.

Uptime band (SLO) | Monthly retainer | Included response window | Credit on SLO miss
99.5% (standard)   | $0 (included)     | 8 business hours         | 10% of monthly retainer
99.9% (priority)   | $3,500            | 2 hours                  | 25% of monthly retainer
99.99% (premium)   | $12,000           | 30 minutes               | 50% of monthly retainer

Surge / uplift windows (e.g., Black Friday event):
- Option A: Timeboxed uplift add-on (7–14 day window): +40% of monthly retainer, reduces response to 15 minutes for premium band, and credits calculated on hourly impact rather than whole-month.
- Option B: Event retainer (flat fee per event) for a single-day peak: $5,000, includes dedicated on-call coverage and one named escalation engineer.

Credits/overage notes:
- Availability credits are calculated pro-rata for the window of failure. For uplift windows we measure credits at an hourly granularity; for standard months we use calendar-day granularity.
- Throughput/latency credits: we differentiate between throttling (where we auto-scale or route) vs sustained capacity exhaust. We provide burst capacity options and bill overages as usage at agreed Tiers or apply a pre-paid token bucket.

Discounting: with a 12-month committed ARR of $250k we can offer 10% off retainer fees and split the implementation fee; 20% available at $500k ARR.

Questions for Tiago:
- What are baseline vs peak RPS? (numbers help us pick the right burst SKU)
- Do you want a named on-call / direct paging during the event? That changes pricing materially.

I can convert this to a table/one-pager and add examples (credit calculations) once we have RPS.

Thanks,

Hi Tiago —

Operational notes on escalation and telemetry:
- Telemetry & auto-assessments: our platform emits incident markers for Availability (HTTP error budget breach), Tail Latency (95/99/99.9), and Queue Saturation. For Availability and clear SLO breaches we auto-calculate credit windows; for tail-latency impacts we require a triage ticket + kernel-level traces to validate root cause before issuing partial credits. The team does proactively surface suspected degradations, but customer claim + telemetry pairing speeds credits.

- Named on-call: If you opt for a named escalation engineer (Option B for event retainer) they join your runbook and are paged directly. That team member will coordinate cross-functional escalations (infra, routing, model fallback). Named on-call is included for the 24–72 hour uplift window when purchased.

- After-hours coverage: our standard 99.9 / 99.99 bands include 24/7 escalation routing; the retainer buys a guaranteed response within the banded window (e.g., 30m for premium). For guaranteed senior-engineer arrival / war-room within 60 minutes we add a one-time mobilization fee ($2,500) per event.

Link to our support runbook and incident checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-support-runbook

Happy to walk through an example credit calc on the call.

Best,
